page: Microsoft Azure E8-4s_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL processor cores operating at 2.6 GHz, with Hyper-Threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes a 50 MB L3 cache, 32 KB L1d cache, and 0.25 MB L2 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU. Local storage consists of a 131 GB volume, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results indicate a clear tradeoff between memory capacity and processing throughput. The server exhibits weak performance in both single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, placing in the bottom 25%. Similarly, PassMark CPU, Geekbench single-core, and Geekbench multi-core scores fall into the bottom 25% category. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks are also weak, though the PassMark memory score achieves an average rating in the middle 50%. Computational tasks such as gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and software compilation with Clang are constrained, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression dropping into the bottom 10%.

For database and application workloads, the server delivers weak performance in Redis SET operations and PassMark database operations, alongside weak static web serving throughput. LLM inference testing with a small 135M model shows weak prompt processing but average text generation speeds. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server provides a dense memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high CPU throughput, such as caching layers, small relational databases, or memory-bound enterprise applications.
